title: Settings installs the Photonz skills for Claude Code and Copilot with one click, from the app alone
goal: Someone with only the Photonz app can turn on 'use Photonz from Claude Code' or 'from GitHub Copilot' in Settings with one Install button each, and an agent in either tool can then drive Photonz. Uninstall is one click too. Today it only installs from a copy of the source, and Copilot isn't supported at all.
notes: User, 2026-10-24: 'I'd love the skills an FRE for using photonz with copilot and claude code where there is a nice explainer and an opt in to install the skills... they can dismiss and install the skills from settings.' This task is the Settings half and the packaging. The setup-window step is a separate task that depends on this one (filed the same minute). Today: Scripts/install-mcp.sh (claude mcp add --scope user, links plugin/skills/photonz into ~/.claude/skills), and there is nothing for Copilot. Focus success gap: agent-mcp success says 'installs with one command'; today that command is Scripts/install-mcp.sh in a checkout (lines 39 and 44: claude mcp add plus a skill link). docs/design/agent-mcp.md 'Not in this slice' (line 392-397): shipping the bridge inside the app bundle. Rough lines in queue/audits/2026-10-19-agent-skill.json ('The install is a developer's') and 2026-10-19-agent-mcp-reach-read-see.json ('builds a small helper program the first time, about 4 seconds'). Skill at plugin/skills/photonz/SKILL.md, plugin/.mcp.json. The channel already listens in every build (agent-mcp.md:34-41, release.sock, dev.sock, probe.sock). Scripts/build-app.sh must copy and sign the helper; never touch dist/Photonz Dev.app from a runner, use the probe.
acceptance: The small server program and the Photonz skill ship inside the app bundle (release, Dev and Probe builds), signed with the app, and codesign --verify --deep passes on the bundle

Settings has an Agents section (place it by the placement contract) with one row per tool, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot (VS Code and the Copilot CLI). Each row says in one line what it gives you, whether that tool was found on this Mac, and has Install / Uninstall. Install registers the Photonz server and puts the skill where that tool reads skills or instructions, with no Terminal and no copied command. Unfound tools say how to get them in one line. A Copy command fallback may stay for people who want it

From a folder with no Photonz source, a fresh session in each tool, installed only through that button, reads the open document and renders a picture from the probe. Proved in the audit for Claude Code and for Copilot, with the session output. If Copilot can only take the server (no skills), say what it gets and give it the skill's instructions in the form it reads. Log what was chosen
Install never overwrites a person's own config: it adds its own entry, and Uninstall removes only that entry. Both are covered by tests against sample config files for each tool
Scripts/install-mcp.sh keeps working for developers and points at the same server; removing works too
The first run builds nothing (today it compiles a helper for about 4 seconds)

Copy is short and plain, no em dashes, no vendor names beyond the two tool names. Works at Next defaults (Agents can work in Photonz is on by default there). Try path: from a folder with no Photonz source, open Settings, press Install on the Claude Code row, start a fresh session and ask it to describe the open picture. Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: triage 2026-10-26: the try path still said "copy the command, run it", which contradicts the one-click Install this task is for; rewritten to press Install. Its notes say it is the Settings half of the user's 2026-10-24 setup ask, which is why it sits among the user's asks.

User, 2026-10-26 intake: 'the mcp server we built has no skill for claude code or copilot bundled and installed with the setup', called 'maybe even more important' than brush performance; moved to the front. Checked from intake: the only installer is still Scripts/install-mcp.sh in a checkout (claude mcp add + a symlink to plugin/skills/photonz); nothing in Sources installs the server or the skill, and nothing exists for Copilot. The skill must ship inside the bundle and be installed with the server, never the server alone.

Review before building: a person with only the app has no claude mcp command to copy and no repo; the installer must find claude/VS Code/copilot without the shell PATH (an app from Finder has none), must not clobber a server or skill of the same name that is not ours, must survive VS Code's mcp.json being JSONC, and the server must reach the app it was installed from (a release user with Dev never installed). Found here: claude at ~/.local/bin, VS Code 1.129 (Copilot built in, its bundled agent reads ~/.copilot/skills), no copilot CLI (a temp copy in /tmp/copilot-cli authenticates with the gh token, for the proof). Copilot CLI reads ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (mcpServers, type local) and personal skills from ~/.copilot/skills; VS Code reads ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json (servers, type stdio).

Chose: Claude Code's server goes in through its own claude mcp add-json/remove (it owns ~/.claude.json, which running sessions rewrite all the time) over editing that file, with the is-it-ours check read from the file first; Copilot's two configs are edited by Photonz (pure transforms in PhotonzCore, tested on sample files), refusing a file with comments rather than rewriting it. One server name per build (photonz, photonz-dev, photonz-probe) so Dev and release install side by side; the bundled bridge reaches the app it sits in unless PHOTONZ_APP says otherwise (a go loop session still gets the probe). The skill is copied (with a marker file) into ~/.claude/skills/photonz and ~/.copilot/skills/photonz.

Built: PhotonzCore AgentSetup (config transforms, ownership, row state; 22 tests on sample Copilot CLI, VS Code and ~/.claude.json files), the bundled bridge reaches its own app (AgentChannelAddress.bundle(containingHelper:), tested), Scripts/build-app.sh copies + signs Contents/Helpers/photonz-mcp and Contents/Resources/AgentSkill/photonz (codesign --verify --deep --strict passes on the probe and release bundles; dev signs the same way as probe), app AgentInstaller + AgentsSettingsSection (Settings > Agents, shown with next-agent-channel, on at Next defaults), walk setup agentHome. Proof: Install pressed on the real buttons via the accessibility tree (a walk press does not reach Settings buttons, filed as a-walk-can-press-the-buttons-in-the-settings-win), then fresh claude -p and copilot -p (Copilot CLI 1.0.104 from /tmp/copilot-cli) sessions in an empty /tmp folder each loaded the photonz skill and called list_documents, read_document, render_picture on the probe: queue/audits/2026-10-26-agents-settings-sessions.md. Uninstall restored ~/.claude.json's servers and VS Code's mcp.json to their backed-up content and removed both skill copies; VS Code's file was then put back byte for byte from the backup, and ~/.copilot (made by my CLI runs, absent before) removed. Bundled bridge with GO_LOOP_PID unset launched and answered from its own probe bundle, never Dev. Scripts/install-mcp.sh --probe and --remove still work. Full suite green (one run had a TitleBackgroundsRenderTests flake that passed alone and on the rerun).

Left rough (not filed): VS Code mcp.json is rewritten in JSONSerialization's formatting (content kept); no shell-PATH lookup for claude/copilot beyond the usual install folders; the installed skill does not refresh itself after an app update (the row offers Update). The first-run setup window half is its own task (the-setup-window-walks-you-through-only-the-step).

Settings > Agents installs and uninstalls the Photonz server and skill for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot (VS Code and the Copilot CLI) with one button each; the bridge and skill ship signed inside every bundle (codesign --verify --deep passes on probe and release). Proved with fresh claude -p and copilot -p sessions from an empty folder that read and rendered the probe's picture (queue/audits/2026-10-26-agents-settings-sessions.md); config transforms tested on sample files; full suite green.
